pairs.why: B's tabletop, plinth and stool tops all share the same downward view and sit on the grass, while A's stool tops look more level than its steeply viewed checkerboard top.
A's yoke grips the clamp and pivots on both sides of the can, but B's yoke has only one pivot on the right and its left arm stops on top of the can without attaching.
B's labeled keys sit in rows that follow its tilted face, while A's blank keys couldn't be used and stay front-facing on the rotated body.
B's craters are shallow dents that follow the rock's surface, while A's 'craters' are deep tunnels that bore through the lump.
B is a complete four-wheeled wagon with a tongue and wheels foreshortened to match the body; A's front wheel faces the viewer while the bed turns away, and its cover has a hole at the back.
A's loop runs through a proper honda eye, so it would work as a lasso, while B's loop is just knotted onto the side of the coil.
B's tail and paws rest flat on the planks with a matching shadow, while A's curled tail hovers a little uncertainly against the floor.
A hangs flat on the wall with a matching shadow, while B is a round clock standing on its rim on the floor with no stand to hold it up.
